questions.questionHtml: For the mid values 30, 39, 48, 57 and 66 the second class of the distribution is ________.

options.html: 34 - 44
34.5 - 43.5

questions.solution:
Given

Mid values = 30, 39, 48, 57, 66

Formula used

Mid value of class interval = (L1 + L2)/2

L1 = Lower limit

L2 = Upper limit

Calculation

For Second class mid value would be (L1 + L2)/2

Here L1 and L2 are Lower value and upper value of class interval

 Mid point of 30 and 39 = (L1 + L2)/2

⇒ (30 + 39)/2 = 34.5

⇒ Mid point of 39 and 48

⇒ (39 + 48)/2 = 43.5

⇒ Lower limit (L1 = 34.5)

⇒ Upper limit (L2 = 43.5)

∴ The second class  of this distribution is 34.5 – 43.5

Shortcut Trick

By options

Class size  44 – 34 = 10

39 – 30  =9

So size gap does not match so option 1 is wrong

2 – 34.5 – 43.5

Class size = 43.5 – 34.5 = 9

The mid point gap

So option (2) match with Class Size so option (2) is correct

questions.question: Calculate skewness using Bowley's formula given lower quartile, upper quartile and median values of a data set are 16, 40 and 24.
questions.questionHtml: Calculate skewness using Bowley's formula given lower quartile, upper quartile and median values of a data set are 16, 40 and 24.
questions.solution:
Given

Q1 = 16

Q3 = 40

Md = 24

Formula 

absolute measure of skewness = = Bowley's measure of skewness Sq = (Q3 - 2Md + Q1)(/Q3 - Q1)

Q1 = Upper quartile

Q3 = Upper quartile

Md = Median

Calculation

Bowley's measure of skewness = (40 + 16 - 2 × 24)/(40 - 16)

⇒ (56 - 48)/24

∴ Bowley's measure of skewness is 8/24 or 0.33

Bowley's measure of skewness = This measure is based on quartiles. For a symmetrical distribution, Q1 and Q3 are equidistance from median

⇒ absolute measure of skewness =  (Q3 - Md) - (Md - Q1)

⇒ A relative measure of skewness is called Bowley's coefficient and it is denotted by SQ

⇒ SQ = [(Q3 - Md) - (Md - Q1)]/[(Q3 - Md) + (Md - Q1)]

⇒ SQ = (Q3 - 2Md + Q1)(/Q3 - Q1)

SK = (Mean – Mode)/Standard deviation

Sk = Karl pearson’s coefficient

Calculation

Karl pearson’s measure of skewness is based upon the divergence of mean from mode in a skewed distribution

Let mean be x

⇒ 0.25 = (x – 18)/6

⇒ x = 0.25 × 6 + 1

⇒ x = 19.5

∴ Mean is 19.5

Index number = (index number for base year/index number of current year) × 100

⇒ Current year = 2016

⇒ Price index = 116

⇒ Price index = (Index of 2016/index of 2011) × 100
